newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran ends subsidies on domestic flights.
newsitem.headline: Iran ends subsidies on domestic flights.

text.p: Iran has stopped subsidising domestic flights, eliminating the last low-budget fares on the flag carrier Iran Air, in a move to restructure the airline, a newspaper and travel agents said on Thursday.
The daily Salam quoted a roads and transport ministry official as saying subsidies for domestic air tickets were to be cut as of October 26.
But travel agents said they had already started to sell tickets at the new rates which raised Iran Air fares by up to three times to the level already charged by other airlines.

The price of an Iran Air ticket from Tehran to the Gulf port city of Bandar Abbas, 1,000 km (600 miles) to the south, was raised to 184,000 rials ($61) from 60,000 rials ($20), a travel agent said. This was the highest increase in fares.
"Not many people were surprised because already it was very difficult to get a quick booking on the few cheaper Iran Air flights," she told Reuters.
Iran Air had in the past few years limited the low fares to a few of its flights, selling seats on most flights at the higher fares through its subsidiary Iran Air Tours.
Iran's other state-run and private airlines raised their rates in July by about 20 percent.

"The two-rate system had caused lots of protests by people who could not get the lower fares. The rate unification was due last year but the president (Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani) postponed it," the official told the newspaper Salam.
Airline officials have repeatedly said the low fares made it impossible for Iran Air to cover costs and gather the capital needed to renew its aging fleet.
($1=3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
